title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA INAUGURATES JAGADGURU KRIPALU UNIVERSITY AT CUTTACK
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau President's Secretariat PRESIDENT OF INDIA INAUGURATES JAGADGURU KRIPALU UNIVERSITY AT CUTTACK OUR UNIVERSITIES MUST CREATE AN ENVIRONMENT WHERE YOUNG PEOPLE CAN DEVELOP THEIR TALENTS AND REALIZE THEIR DREAMS AND ASPIRATIONS: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the Jagadguru Kripalu University at Cuttack, Odisha today (August 3, 2026). Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Odisha has been a land with a rich tradition of knowledge, culture, spirituality and service. For centuries, this sacred land of Mahaprabhu Jagannath has spread the message of inclusivity, compassion and human welfare. The region of Cuttack is the birthplace of great luminaries such as 'Utkal Gourav' Madhusudan Das, 'Karmavir' Gauri Shankar Ray, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose, and Biju Patnaik. It is also the workplace for 'Utkalmani' Pandit Gopabandhu Das and 'Utkal Kesari' Dr. Harekrushna Mahtab. Cuttack’s contribution to the fields of public service, literature, and culture has been immensely significant and inspiring. It is expected that the Jagadguru Kripalu University, established in such a glorious region, will serve as a powerful medium for the service of society and the nation by integrating India's ancient cultural and spiritual traditions with modern education. The President said that India is among the countries with the youngest populations in the world. This is our greatest asset. To make optimal use of this asset, our universities must create an environment where young people can develop their talents and realize their dreams and aspirations. They must be provided with value-based education. Universities bear the responsibility of shaping citizens guided by integrity, discipline, sensitivity and a commitment to the national interest. She stated that the knowledge acquired by the youth becomes truly meaningful only when it is used in the service of humanity, the welfare of society, and the progress of the nation. The President said that we have set a goal to build Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. Our higher education institutions play a pivotal role in achieving this objective. She urged universities to function as centres of knowledge where the ideas and technologies developed address the needs of society. She said that while embracing modern knowledge, students should remain committed to ethical values. She was happy to note that Jagadguru Kripalu University will foster research, innovation, and entrepreneurship while emphasizing the cultural and spiritual growth of students. She expressed confidence that this university will produce skilled manpower, researchers, and entrepreneurs who will contribute to realizing the goals of a ‘Viksit Odisha’ and a ‘Viksit Bharat’. title: MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF UZBEKISTAN CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau President's Secretariat MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF UZBEKISTAN CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 3:02PM by PIB Delhi H.E. Mr Saidov Bakhtiyor Odilovich, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan, called on the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (August 3, 2026). Welcoming Mr Odilovich and his delegation to Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President said that India and Uzbekistan share deep historical, cultural, and civilizational ties, rooted in ancient trade routes. She highlighted that the shared heritage in architecture, language, cuisine, music, and religious traditions has further strengthened bilateral partnership. The President said that the presence of high-level leaders in the visiting Uzbek delegation and the organisation of an India-Uzbekistan Business Forum on the sidelines of the visit reflect the growing confidence of businesses of both sides in each other's markets. She also highlighted the immense potential for cooperation between India and Uzbekistan in the mining sector, particularly in rare earth minerals, agriculture, pharmaceuticals, and information technology. The President was happy to note that more than 3,000 officials, professionals and students from Uzbekistan have benefited from our ITEC training courses and other scholarship programs. At the same time over 16,000 Indian students are pursuing higher studies in Uzbekistan. She underlined that they act as a bridge between the two countries and foster mutual understanding and strong people-to-people ties. The two leaders agreed that discussions held during this visit will further strengthen the bonds of friendship, trust, and cooperation between our two nations. *** MJPS/SS/PRK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293746) आगंतुक पटल  : 510 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Bengali , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Malayalam President's Secretariat MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF UZBEKISTAN CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Text of the felicitation remarks delivered by the Hon'ble Chairman on the outstanding achievement of the Indian Contingent at the Commonwealth Games and the Commonwealth Para Games on 03-08-2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Rajya Sabha Secretariat Text of the felicitation remarks delivered by the Hon'ble Chairman on the outstanding achievement of the Indian Contingent at the Commonwealth Games and the Commonwealth Para Games on 03-08-2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi CHAIRMAN : Hon'ble Members, the House joins me in congratulating the Indian contingent on its outstanding performance at the just concluded Commonwealth Games and the Commonwealth Para Games held at Glasgow in Scotland, United Kingdom. India secured an impressive fourth position in the Commonwealth Games medal tally, winning 39 medals overall, comprising 13 Gold, 17 Silver and 9 Bronze medals. Our para-athletes scripted history by registering their best-ever performance at the Commonwealth Para Games with 7 medals, including 3 Gold, 2 Silver and 2 Bronze medals. The remarkable achievement has brought immense pride and honour to the nation and bear testimony to the growing excellence of Indian sportspersons. On behalf of the House and on my own behalf, I extend our heartiest congratulations to all the athletes, coaches, support staff, the Indian Olympic Association, the Paralympic Committee of India and the National Sports Federations. Our medal winners will surely serve as an inspiration, not only to the budding sporting talent in our country, but also to every young Indian to pursue excellence through hard work, discipline, determination and perseverance. This House wishes our sportspersons continued success to bring even greater glory to Bharat in the years ahead. **** RKK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294008) आगंतुक पटल  : 83 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati Rajya Sabha Secretariat Text of the felicitation remarks delivered by the Hon'ble Chairman on the outstanding achievement of the Indian Contingent at the Commonwealth Games and the Commonwealth Para Games on 03-08-2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Sonepur Bazari OCP: Setting New Benchmarks in Coal Production and Operational Excellence
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Coal Sonepur Bazari OCP: Setting New Benchmarks in Coal Production and Operational Excellence प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi Situated in the eastern part of the Raniganj Coalfield in Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal, Sonepur Bazari Opencast Mine (OCP) is one of the flagship mines of Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) and among the most productive opencast mines in Coal India Limited (CIL). For decades, the mine has been a vital contributor to India's energy security by supplying quality thermal coal to major power utilities including NTPC, WBPDCL, DVC, CESC and several core industries. With its robust infrastructure, scientific mine planning and operational excellence, Sonepur Bazari continues to play a pivotal role in supporting the nation's growing energy requirements. Outstanding Physical Performance in FY 2026–27 Sonepur Bazari OC has commenced FY 2026–27 with remarkable operational performance, reflecting meticulous planning and efficient execution. Against an ambitious Annual Action Plan (AAP) target of 120 lakh tonnes of coal production, the mine has consistently remained ahead of schedule. Up to the current period, against a planned coal production target of 27.74 lakh tonnes , the mine has produced 29.22 lakh tonnes , achieving 105.34% of the target. This impressive performance is a testimony to efficient resource deployment, disciplined mine planning and strong execution at the field level. Equally noteworthy has been the mine's performance in Overburden Removal (OBR) , which forms the backbone of sustainable coal production. Against a planned OBR target of 206.20 lakh cubic metres , the mine has achieved 253.40 lakh cubic metres , registering an outstanding 122.89% achievement. The accelerated overburden removal has substantially enhanced coal exposure, creating a strong production base for the remaining part of the financial year. The mine has also registered excellent performance in coal evacuation. Coal dispatch during the current financial year has reached 39.94 lakh tonnes , representing a 16% increase over the corresponding period of the previous year. This reflects efficient logistics management, improved evacuation systems and seamless coordination between production and dispatch operations. Major Enabling Conditions for Achieving the Annual Target The impressive operational performance has been backed by several enabling factors that have significantly strengthened the mine's production capability. Recognizing that land availability is the key driver of opencast mining , Sonepur Bazari has made substantial progress in rehabilitation and resettlement, resulting in the successful shifting of villages from coal-bearing areas. This has made available significant mining area, strengthened coal availability and created adequate working faces for sustained production. Simultaneously, additional mining areas have become available, ensuring continuity of operations and providing sufficient operational flexibility to achieve the Annual Action Plan target. Another major strength of the mine is its robust coal evacuation infrastructure. The modern 12 million tonne per annum Coal Handling Plant (CHP) , commissioned in 2021, is equipped with Rapid Loading Systems, twin silos and substantial bunker capacity, enabling dispatch of 10–12 railway rakes per day . This ensures uninterrupted evacuation of coal to consumers across the country and eliminates logistics as a potential bottleneck. The availability of the requisite statutory clearances further reinforces the mine's production readiness. Technology and Infrastructure Driving Productivity Sonepur Bazari possesses one of the most comprehensive fleets of Heavy Earth Moving Machinery (HEMM) in Eastern Coalfields Limited. The mine operates a high-capacity Marion Dragline , electric rope shovels, hydraulic excavators, large-capacity dumpers and a wide range of supporting equipment. Departmental operations are effectively complemented by outsourced mining fleets, ensuring operational flexibility, optimum equipment utilization and high productivity. The mine has also embraced modern mining technologies to enhance productivity while promoting sustainable mining practices. High-capacity Surface Miners enable blast-free coal extraction with improved productivity, uniform coal sizing and lower environmental impact. Advanced drilling systems, controlled blasting techniques and dust suppression measures further contribute to safer and more environmentally responsible mining operations. A Mine Ready to Deliver Sonepur Bazari OCP exemplifies the transformation underway across Coal India Limited's mining operations. Outstanding production performance, exceptional overburden achievement, enhanced coal exposure, improved land availability, world-class infrastructure and adoption of advanced technologies have collectively positioned the mine for another successful year. With all major enabling conditions firmly in place, Sonepur Bazari is confidently poised to achieve its 120 lakh tonne coal production target for FY 2026–27 . More importantly, it demonstrates how sound mine planning, timely execution, technological modernization and a committed workforce can consistently deliver operational excellence. As one of ECL's flagship mines, Sonepur Bazari continues to set new benchmarks in productivity while making a significant contribution to Coal India Limited's mission of ensuring reliable, affordable and sustainable energy security for the nation. **** Shuhaib T (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293791) आगंतुक पटल  : 313 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Coal Sonepur Bazari OCP: Setting New Benchmarks in Coal Production and Operational Excellence प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Monthly Production and Dispatch from Captive and Commercial Mines Continue Upward Growth in July 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Coal Monthly Production and Dispatch from Captive and Commercial Mines Continue Upward Growth in July 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 12:21PM by PIB Delhi Maintaining its strong growth trajectory, the Captive and Commercial coal mining sector continued to deliver higher production in July 2026, reinforcing its growing role in India's coal ecosystem. During the month, coal production from Captive and Commercial mines stood at 14.78 million tonnes (MT), while coal dispatches reached 17.49 MT. Coal production registered a 9.61% year-on-year growth compared to July 2025, reflecting sustained momentum in mining operations and the increasing contribution of these mines to the country's domestic coal output. The encouraging performance highlights continued improvements in operational efficiency, enhanced mining productivity, and more effective utilisation of mining capacities across the Captive and Commercial coal mining sector. The accompanying graph illustrates the production and dispatch performance during the month (in million tonnes). The sustained rise in production from Captive and Commercial mines is expected to reduce dependence on imported coal, strengthen supply chain resilience, conserve valuable foreign exchange, and advance the Government's vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat by enhancing self-reliance in a critical raw material essential for the nation's energy security and industrial development. The Ministry of Coal remains committed to fully unlocking the potential of the Captive and Commercial coal mining sector. It will continue to sustain production growth, address supply-side constraints, and improve coal availability through progressive policy interventions, robust regulatory oversight, and continued stakeholder support, while ensuring that the sector makes a reliable contribution towards meeting the nation's growing energy and industrial requirements. **** Shuhaib T (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293622) आगंतुक पटल  : 582 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Coal Monthly Production and Dispatch from Captive and Commercial Mines Continue Upward Growth in July 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Shri Piyush Goyal Invites Indian and Uzbek Businesses to Co-invest and Co-manufacture; Calls for Doubling Bilateral Trade at India-Uzbekistan Business Forum
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Invites Indian and Uzbek Businesses to Co-invest and Co-manufacture; Calls for Doubling Bilateral Trade at India-Uzbekistan Business Forum Shri Goyal Highlights Investment Opportunities in Mining and Textiles; Says Bilateral Investment Treaty Will Boost India-Uzbekistan Partnerships Shri Goyal Calls for Expanding India-Uzbekistan Cooperation in Healthcare, Agriculture, Digital Technologies and Advanced Manufacturing प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 2:11PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today invited businesses from India and Uzbekistan to co-invest, co-manufacture and co-innovate, while calling for concerted efforts to double bilateral trade between the two countries over the next three years. Addressing the India-Uzbekistan Business Forum in New Delhi, the Minister said the strategic partnership between the two countries, founded on mutual trust, respect and a shared vision for prosperity, offers tremendous opportunities for expanding trade, investment and economic cooperation. Welcoming the delegation, Shri Goyal said India and Uzbekistan are bound not only by a rich shared history and deep cultural connect, but also by immense business potential that remains largely untapped. He observed that while bilateral trade has crossed approximately USD 1.5 billion, it represents only a fraction of what the two economies can achieve together. The Minister said India offers Uzbekistan not only a large and growing market but also a reliable partner, a skilled and youthful workforce and a platform for innovation-led growth. Referring to the recently concluded Bilateral Investment Treaty between India and Uzbekistan, he said the agreement would enhance investor confidence and encourage businesses from both countries to invest in each other's economies and build long-term partnerships. Shri Goyal identified several sectors with strong complementarities that offer significant scope for bilateral collaboration. He said Uzbekistan presents substantial opportunities for Indian investment in the mining sector. He also highlighted the potential for cooperation in textiles, noting Uzbekistan's strength in cotton production and India's leadership in the textile industry, with opportunities to jointly expand into garment manufacturing, design and global markets. In the pharmaceutical and healthcare sectors, the Minister said India, recognised as the pharmacy of the world, can support Uzbekistan's healthcare modernisation through affordable medicines, medical devices, diagnostics, telemedicine, training of doctors and paramedics, and quality healthcare services. He also proposed reviving cooperation in traditional systems of medicine such as Ayurveda, Yoga and Unani, which had historical links with the Uzbek region. On agriculture and food processing, Shri Goyal said cooperation in food processing, packaging, cold chains and agri-tech could help build global value chains that benefit farmers in both countries while serving international markets through complementary strengths. The Minister also underlined India's readiness to collaborate with Uzbekistan in information technology and the digital economy. He said India would be happy to work with Uzbekistan in developing Digital Public Infrastructure and strengthening cooperation in areas such as fintech, agri-tech and medtech. He further noted that engineering components, advanced manufacturing, automotive components and automobiles also offer promising avenues for future collaboration. The Minister noted that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the President of Uzbekistan H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev have imparted new dynamism to bilateral relations by bringing the people of the two countries closer together and providing a clear political direction for the partnership. He emphasised that the full potential of the relationship can be realised only when businesses from both sides deepen engagement, expand economic ties, increase investments and create more employment opportunities. Emphasising that trade must lead the bilateral relationship, Shri Goyal urged businesses to seize the opportunity to build enduring commercial partnerships. He called for eliminating trade barriers, promoting mutual recognition of standards, approvals, testing and certification processes, integrating customs systems through greater digitalisation, and creating more efficient trade routes to facilitate commerce. title: Department of Posts releases Commemorative Postage Stamp to Mark the Centenary of Satish Gujral
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications Department of Posts releases Commemorative Postage Stamp to Mark the Centenary of Satish Gujral Postage stamps carry the soul of the country and preserve India's cultural legacy for generations: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Posts today released a Commemorative Postage Stamp on the Centenary of renowned artist, architect, sculptor, muralist and writer late Shri Satish Gujral at a special ceremony held at Bikaner House, New Delhi. The stamp was released by the Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia , in the presence of Director General Postal Services, Shri Jitendra Gupta , Chief Postmaster General Delhi Circle Col. Akhilesh Kumar Pandey , famous Indian painter, sculptor, and muralist Padma Bhushan recipient Shri Jatin Das , former Director General of the National Gallery of Modern Art Dr. Rajeev Lochan , Ms. Raseel Gujral Ansal , members of the Gujral family and other distinguished guests. Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia releases the Commemorative Postage Stamp on the Centenary of late Shri Satish Gujral with Dr. Rajeev Lochan, Mr. Jatin Das, Ms. Raseel Gujral Ansal, and Navin Ansal. Addressing the gathering, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia described late Shri Satish Gujral as a creative genius whose life reflected resilience, innovation and excellence. He highlighted Gujral's extraordinary contributions as a painter, sculptor, architect, muralist and writer, noting that his works continue to inspire generations in India and across the world. Recalling late Shri Satish Gujral's long and cherished association with the Department of Posts, the Union Minister noted that the celebrated artist not only created works of art but also transformed ideas into powerful visual narratives through his stamp designs. Referring to the commemorative stamp issued on the 125th anniversary of VSNL , he observed that Gujral had translated the idea of communication into striking visual metaphors. Likewise, in the Financial Inclusion stamp, he brought together the themes of progress, empowerment and national development through evocative symbolism rather than literal imagery. Emphasizing the enduring significance of postage stamps, the Union Minister said, "Postage stamps are very small in size, but they carry the soul of our country. They carry the passion of 140 crore people, travelling from city to city, village to village, taluk to taluk, carrying India’s history, culture and collective memories across generations." He expressed confidence that the commemorative stamp would preserve Satish Gujral's legacy and inspire future generations. The stamp features a portrait of late Shri Satish Gujral seated with a paintbrush held prominently in his hand, symbolising his lifelong passion for art and creativity. The composition highlights him in a thoughtful pose, reflecting the depth and versatility of his artistic vision. Set against a vibrant artistic backdrop inspired by his distinctive style rendered in rich shades of purple and blue, the design conveys a sense of dignity and creative expression. The stamp has been designed by Shri Anuj Kumar on the proposal of Ms. Raseel Gujral Ansal. Late Shri Satish Gujral was one of India's most distinguished creative luminaries whose career spanned over seven decades. A recipient of the Padma Vibhushan, he made significant contributions to Indian art, architecture and culture, leaving behind a legacy that continues to inspire artists worldwide. The commemorative postage stamp celebrates his life, achievements and enduring contribution to India's cultural heritage. title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted through its appointed agency across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA, during the month of July 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). The performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters, captured during IDT are published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Bhopal. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area/ route under test on the day/ time of conducting the drive test. The drive tests conducted across City drive – 292.3 KMs, Hotspot locations - 7, Walk Test - 1.4 KMs, in Haridwar and Rishikesh Cities & nearby areas during 29 th June 2026 to 1 st July 2026 in UP West LSA. Drive Test Route Map : The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating C ity drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots and Walk tests, as per the legends shown on the map: - Key Parameters Assessed Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G). Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence (Mute) Rate, Speech Quality (MOS). Call Silence (Mute) Instance : Number of call silence (Mute) instance occurred during the calls. Data Servies: Download/ Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate The overall mobile network performance in Haridwar and Rishikesh city for the key parameters has been summarised below: - a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1534 / 50508 for Airtel , 3920 / 49983 for BSNL , 2699 / 50069 for RJIL and 952 / 50338 for VIL for Haridwar and Rishikesh City . Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map Annexed . b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls, measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 10 / 430 for Airtel , 13 / 426 for BSNL , 2 / 453 for RJIL and 0 / 451 for VIL for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map A nnexed . c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances, measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 9 / 414 for Airtel , 21/ 408 for BSNL , 18 / 435 for RJIL and 12 / 451 for VIL for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map Annexed . d) Data Download and Upload Throughput : i) Data Download performance (Overall) : Average download speed was observed as 128.99 Mbps for Airtel (5G) , 7.96 Mbps for BSNL (4G) , 205.57 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 58.46 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map Annexed. ii) Data Upload performance (Overall) : Average upload speed was observed as 24.54 Mbps for Airtel (5G) , 4.11 Mbps for BSNL (4G) , 23.21 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 14.79 Mbps for VIL (5G) for Haridwar and Rishikesh City. Detail of Upload throughput has been provided in the map Annexed. Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map Annexed. Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT is as under: - City - The areas covered in the city drive are Doiwala, Jolly Grant, Rishikesh, Tapovan, Veerbhadra, Nepali Farm, Raiwala, Haridwar, Jwalapur, Bahadrabad, Salempur Mahdood, Devpura, Ranipur and Sitapur etc. in Haridwar & Rishikesh city. Hotspot - The hot spot locations, capturing stationary user experience, are District Collectorate Office - Haridwar, Gurukul Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Haridwar Railway Station, Jolly Grant Airport - Dehradun, Raiwala Junction Railway Station, Rishikesh Bus Stand, Yog Nagari Rishikesh Railway Station. Walk Test - The walk tests conducted on 29 th June & 1 st July 2026, covered Har Ki Pauri Ganga Ghat - Haridwar, Triveni Ganga Ghat – Rishikesh capturing mobile network behaviour in crowded pedestrian environments. The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs’ for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in For any clarification or additional information, an email can be sent to adv.bhopal@trai.gov.in or regional office of TRAI at Bhopal RO can be contacted on Phone no. +91-755-2575501 Click here to see Annexure ***** NJ/ARJ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293968) आगंतुक पटल  : 91 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Communications TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Haridwar and Rishikesh City under UPW LSA प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia to convene Investors’ Meet along with MP CM Mohan Yadav to attract Investment for Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia to convene Investors’ Meet along with MP CM Mohan Yadav to attract Investment for Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior India’s First TMZ eyes ₹10,000 Crore in Investments; Mumbai Investors’ Meet Set to Accelerate Investment Momentum प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 5:49PM by PIB Mumbai Mumbai : 3 August 2026 Building on the momentum of the launch of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Jyotiraditya M. Scindia will convene a Telecom Manufacturing Zone Investors Meet in Mumbai on 4 August 2026 along with the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Mohan Yadav; Secretary of Department of Telecom, Amit Agarwal and Additional Chief Secretary, Madhya Pradesh Govt., Neeraj Mandloi. The first roadshow and the Investors’ Meet in Mumbai comes close on the heels of the landmark launch of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India and the Government of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July 2026. The TMZ launch was followed by the first Investors’ Roundtable in the national capital. Minister Scindia announced investment commitments of ₹3,500 crore were secured with the potential to generate nearly 14,000 employment opportunities, reflecting the strong confidence of industry in India’s growing telecom manufacturing ecosystem. The Mumbai Investors’ Meet and roadshow marks the next phase of this national initiative to mobilise greater industry participation and investments for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone. It will bring together leading telecom manufacturers, technology companies, infrastructure providers, component manufacturers and investors to accelerate the development of a world-class telecom manufacturing ecosystem in the country. The expected investment in India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone is expected to cross ₹10,000 Crore mark. The establishment of India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone is a landmark stride towards realising the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat in the telecommunications sector. By creating an integrated ecosystem for manufacturing, research and development, design, testing and innovation, the TMZ aims to strengthen domestic value chains, reduce import dependence, promote indigenous manufacturing, boost exports and position India as a trusted global hub for telecom products and next-generation technologies. The enthusiastic response from industry at the inaugural Investors’ Roundtable underscored the transformative potential of the initiative. Leading companies and several telecom industry leaders, committed significant investments towards the project, reaffirming their confidence in India’s policy framework and manufacturing capabilities. The Mumbai Investors’ Meet is expected to further deepen industry partnerships and attract fresh investments, reinforcing the Government’s commitment to building a globally competitive telecom manufacturing ecosystem and transforming India into a leading global destination for telecom manufacturing and innovation. The event will bring together senior government officials, industry leaders, investors and key stakeholders from the telecommunications sector. title: TRAI revamps 'TRAI MyCall' mobile application to assess voice call quality through consumer feedback
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications TRAI revamps 'TRAI MyCall' mobile application to assess voice call quality through consumer feedback प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today launched revamped version of "TRAI MyCall' , a mobile application that enables telecom consumers to directly assess and report the voice-calling experience. TRAI MyCall is a citizen-centric digital platform that empowers telecom consumers share real-time feedback on their voice-calling experience, along with relevant network parameters. The feedback provided by consumers is visible to Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) as well as TRAI in anonymised form. This feedback provides valuable insights to TSPs, helping them identify areas where network performance needs improvement and take targeted corrective measures. This consumer-driven approach is expected to enhance the overall Quality of Service (QoS). The platform also strengthens evidence-based regulatory oversight by enabling TRAI to assess the Quality of Experience (QoE) across telecom networks based on real consumer feedback. With over one billion telecom subscribers in India, voice calling continues to be the most fundamental telecom service and is often the first indicator of network quality experienced by consumers. While network performance is evaluated using technical Quality of Service (QoS) parameters, the Quality of Experience (QoE) perceived by consumers also provides an important perspective on service performance. TRAI MyCall bridges this gap by combining consumer feedback with relevant network information to facilitate a more comprehensive assessment of telecom service quality. The revamped TRAI MyCall application offers several consumer-friendly features, including: Instant rating of voice calls through a simple 1-5 star feedback system. Reporting of specific issues such as call drops, echo during calls, audio delay, cross connection, voice breaking, one party unable to hear the other, and calls taking too long to connect, which shall be available to respective service provider for corrective action. Automatic post-call feedback prompts for seamless participation. Rating and feedback history on interactive map. Coverage Test feature to assess signal strength. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Anil Kumar Lahoti, Chairman, TRAI, said “Every telecom consumer experiences network quality first-hand. The revamped TRAI MyCall app is expected to strengthen consumer participation feedback on telecom service quality by enabling subscribers to provide immediate and perceived feedback on their call experience. The feedback will assist Telecom Service Providers in identifying network deficiencies and taking corrective measures, enhanced customer satisfaction, and a better overall mobile communication experience. The initiative reinforces TRAI's commitment to a consumer-centric, transparent, and data-driven approach to improving the quality of telecom services. I encourage all mobile users to download the TRAI MyCall application and regularly share their feedback. Every feedback matters, and together we can build a better calling experience for every telecom consumer.” TRAI MyCall application can be installed on Android devices from Google Play at following link: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.trai.mycall TRAI remains committed to fostering a transparent, accountable and consumer-responsive telecom ecosystem, with consumer participation playing a central role in strengthening the quality of telecom services. title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF MUSEUMS AND CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF MUSEUMS AND CULTURAL INSTITUTIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Culture is taking different initiatives in digital archiving and collection management to preserve our cultural assets through digitization with JATAN software, developed by C-DAC, Pune, for digitization of museum collections and archival resources. A national digital repository has been created through the Museums of India portal, where digitized collections of eight National Level Museums, two ASI Site Museums and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Museum, Pune are available. Digitized Articles till date can be viewed by accessing the following link: https://museumsofindia.gov.in/repository The Gyan Bharatam Mission , launched under the Ministry of Culture, aims to safeguard India’s vast manuscript heritage and revive its civilizational knowledge traditions for future generations. More than 3.5 lakh digitized manuscripts are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at present for public access, which can be viewed by accessing the following link: https://gyanbharatam.com/ Digitization of archival records are undertaken by the National Archives of India under the Ministry of Culture to preserve valuable documentary heritage and facilitate wider access to archival records. The archival records are regularly uploaded on NAI's dedicated portal, 'Abhilekh Patal' for researchers, scholars and the general public. Statistics are available on the portal at https://www.abhilekh-patal.in/ Birla Industrial & Technological Museum (BITM), Kolkata, a constituent unit of NCSM developed a National Science & Technology Digital Archive containing papers, letters & manuscripts of eminent Indian scientists which was opened on 05.12.2024. URL: https://nstad.in/home-login/ The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) has been undertaking extensive initiatives for the digital preservation, documentation and dissemination of India’s cultural heritage through its various knowledge repositories and digital platforms. IGNCA has developed and maintained comprehensive digital archives covering manuscripts, photographs, rare books, audio-visual recordings, cultural documentation, art objects and archival collections. The details of digitized data for National Level Museums under the Ministry of Culture is attached at Annexure – I National Council of Science Museums (NCSM) under the Ministry of Culture is at the forefront of research and development (R&D) in museum display technologies, continuously innovating to enhance visitor engagement. By integrating cutting-edge technologies such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision and sensor-based interaction. NCSM’s R&D efforts focus on developing intuitive and immersive exhibits that blend seamlessly into the visitor experience. These include advancements in motion tracking, eye-tracking, smart content adaptation and touch less interaction. The goal is to make learning more dynamic, personalized and accessible to all audiences. Indian Museum, Kolkata aligning with the vision of Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi and in accordance with its mandate of promoting and preserving cultural heritage, it has undertaken collaborative initiatives with the academic institutions to strengthen heritage conservation and digital innovation. Indian Museum has joined hands with IIT, Kharagpur for the use of AI based restoration of archaeological artefacts for digital preservation of its collections. Centre for Cultural Resources and Training ( CCRT) , an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Culture, regularly organizes training programmes for teachers, teacher educators and students with the objective of preserving and promoting Indian culture through education. As part of these programmes, educational visits to museums, heritage monuments and nature parks are organized in collaboration with museums and other cultural institutions to facilitate experiential learning and heritage awareness. Institutions include National Museum, National Gallery of Modern Art, National Crafts Museum & Hastkala Academy, National Science Centre, Gandhi Smriti and Darshan Samiti, Swachhata Kendra, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb and Red Fort in Delhi. Similar collaborations are undertaken through CCRT Regional Centres for visits to the Salar Jung Museum (Hyderabad), Bhartiya Lok Kala Mandal (Udaipur), Assam State Museum (Guwahati) and Rani Damayanti Archaeological Museum (Damoh). Digital documentation of antiquities and built heritage sites of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has been undertaken through the National Mission оn Monuments Antiquities (NMMA). Further, 723 antiquities of the ASI Museum, Goa and 8,450 antiquities of the ASI Museum, Nagarjunakonda have been digitally documented and uploaded on the JATAN software developed by C-DAC, Pune in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture. MoC has undertaken the following steps to enhance technology-enabled visitor experience and digital access including: Digitization of manuscripts, photographs and archival collections. Online access to selected publications and archival resources. Digital documentation of tangible and intangible cultural heritage. Use of multimedia and interactive technologies during exhibitions, conferences and outreach programmes. These initiatives have substantially improved accessibility to cultural resources for researchers, students and the public. National Council of Science Museums (NCSM) under the Ministry of Culture being the apex body of science museums/centres with 26 units in different parts of the country as listed at Annexure-II , houses exhibit which are basically hands on and participatory in nature and are developed in house. NCSM prepares a well thought Annual Action Plan as per periodic requirement every year for upgradation, renovation and modernization of museums and centres under its control to enhance the visitor experience including Palampur Science Centre, Palampur in the state of Himachal Pradesh. Further, under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS) , (details of the scheme can be found in ( https://www.indianculture.gov.in/ ) NCSM has undertaken modernization/upgradation of six (6) Science Centres in various parts of the country namely: - Ranchi Science Centre, Jharkhand; Sukanta Academy of Arts, Science & Culture, Tripura; Nagaland Science Centre, Dimapur; Shillong Science Centre, Meghalaya; Mizoram Science Centre, Aizawl and Manipur Science Centre, Manipur. Indian Museum in collaboration with Google Art & Culture has prepared a virtual exhibition for promotion of heritage through digital interventions. As a part of its modernisation, AI-based interactives and AR-based visitor engagement tools have been introduced to provide immersive gallery experience to the visitors. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has launched mobile-based applications for the Archaeological Museums at Hampi (Karnataka) and Nalanda (Bihar). The applications provide virtual tours of the museums and facilitate digital access to the artefacts displayed therein. IGNCA has undertaken documentation, research, publication and digital preservation of various aspects of Mithila art, traditions and manuscripts through its regular academic and archival activities. title: Gyan Bharatam Mission and Preservation of Manuscript Heritage
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture Gyan Bharatam Mission and Preservation of Manuscript Heritage प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi Gyan Bharatam Mission (GBM), announced during Union Budget 2025-26, is an initiative of the Ministry of Culture (MoC), Government of India to undertake manuscripts related activities. The objectives of this initiative are as follows: To leverage advanced technology to significantly enhance the pace of digitization and documentation of manuscripts. Conducting survey and registration of manuscripts. To document and catalogue Indian manuscripts, wherever they may be, maintain accurate and up-to-date information about them and the conditions under which they may be conserved. To facilitate usage of manuscripts and promote ready access to these manuscripts through publications, both in book form as well as machine readable form. To facilitate conservation and preservation of manuscripts through training awareness and financial support. To boost scholarship and research in the study of Indian languages and manuscriptology. To build up a National Digital Repository (NDR). To support the initiative, the Standing Finance Committee (SFC) has sanctioned Rs.491.66 crore for the period 2025-2031. National Manuscript Survey was launched in March, 2026 across all States and Union Territories (UTs) of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories and custodians representing diverse languages and scripts. During the survey, more than 1.19 crore manuscripts have been reported. The total number of digitized manuscripts available across the country is over 8 lakh, out of which, more than 4.40 lakh manuscripts are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at present for public access, in view mode which is accessible state-wise. The mission has established an institutional mechanism through Cluster Centres and Independent Centres which include universities, research institutions, libraries, archives, private custodians, religious institutions, and other stakeholders to undertake manuscript related activities. States / Union Territories (UTs) have also been engaged to act as Nodal Coordinating Authority for Gyan Bharatam implementation within the State / UT concerned. Access to digitized copies of manuscript is facilitated in accordance with the rights of custodians and rights holders. Wherever permissible, manuscripts and associated metadata may be made available for public and scholarly research through the National Digital Repository, while sensitive, restricted or rights-protected materials may be subject to appropriate access conditions. GBM is a pan-India initiative aimed at preserving India’s manuscript heritage, irrespective of script, language, knowledge tradition, region, or the custodial traditions of communities. Institutions located in Bihar namely (i) Nava Nalanda Mahavihar, Nalanda (ii) Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Public Library, Patna and (iii) Shri Bodh Gaya Math, Bodh Gaya have onboarded with GBM to undertake manuscript related activities. This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. *** M Annadurai (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293807) आगंतुक पटल  : 368 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Culture Gyan Bharatam Mission and Preservation of Manuscript Heritage प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: VICE ADMIRAL MANISH CHADHA, AVSM, VSM, ASSUMES CHARGE AS DIRECTOR GENERAL NAVAL OPERATIONS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence VICE ADMIRAL MANISH CHADHA, AVSM, VSM, ASSUMES CHARGE AS DIRECTOR GENERAL NAVAL OPERATIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi Vice Admiral Manish Chadha, AVSM, VSM, assumed charge as the Director General Naval Operations on 03 Aug 26 . An alumnus of the 78th course of the National Defence Academy, Khadakwasla, Vice Admiral Manish Chadha was commissioned into the Indian Navy on 01 Jul 1991. The Flag Officer is a Communication and Electronic Warfare Specialist. He is an alumnus of the 61st Defence Services Staff College, Wellington, and completed the Higher Command Course at the National Defence University, Washington, USA. In a distinguished career spanning over 35 years, the Flag Officer has held a wide range of command, operational, instructional, and staff appointments, both afloat and ashore. His key afloat appointments include command of Coast Guard Interceptor Boat CGS-05 and Indian Naval Ships Veer, Kirpan, and Mysore. The Flag Officer also served as the Naval Attaché at the Embassy of India, Moscow. At Naval Headquarters, he steered several key projects, including projects for VLF and satellite communications, besides serving as the Director, International Fleet Review 2016. title: CDS Addresses Participants at the Fourth Edition of Tri-Services Future Warfare Course
content:

                03 AUG 2026 6:17PM by PIB Delhi The Fourth Edition of the Tri-Services Future Warfare Course commenced at the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi on August 03, 2026, with the Chief of the Defence Staff (CDS), General N.S. Raja Subramani, delivering the keynote address at the inaugural session. In his address, the CDS focused on the changing character of warfare and the growing influence of emerging technologies on military operations. He emphasised the importance of anticipating future security challenges and developing the ability to respond effectively across multiple operational domains. The CDS highlighted the increasing role of artificial intelligence, cyber capabilities, autonomous systems, information warfare, space technologies and data-driven decision-making in shaping future conflicts. He also stressed the need for greater jointness, integration and collaboration between the Armed Forces, industry, academia and the research community to strengthen national defence preparedness. Conducted by the Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS), this four-week course will bring together officers from the three Services along with representatives from government, industry, academia and strategic institutions. During the programme, participants will deliberate on subjects covering geopolitics, emerging technologies, cognitive and cyber warfare, multi-domain operations, scenario-building and technology-enabled warfare. ********* SR/ Kamlesh (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293950) आगंतुक पटल  : 151 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Defence CDS Addresses Participants at the Fourth Edition of Tri-Services Future Warfare Course प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Military-civil integration key to a robust defence ecosystem to tackle emerging challenges: Raksha Mantri at AFHQ Civilian Services Day celebrations
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence Military-civil integration key to a robust defence ecosystem to tackle emerging challenges: Raksha Mantri at AFHQ Civilian Services Day celebrations “‘Nation First’ a shared commitment of uniformed & civil services; Every element transforms into national strength if the objective is one” “AFHQ Civilian Services must evolve into strategic brain of India’s defence management; Research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas vital for strengthening national security” प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi As the Defence Forces are marching towards greater jointness with renewed vigour, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has underlined the need to deepen integration between the military and civil components of the Ministry of Defence to foster greater synergy within the defence ecosystem to tackle evolving security & technological challenges, while ensuring institutional memory, stability, and the effective application of rules and regulations. A ddressing the 85th Armed Forces Headquarters (AFHQ) Civilian Services Day celebrations in New Delhi on August 03, 2026, he emphasised that both the uniformed and civil services share the same commitment of ‘Nation First’, and when the objective is singular, every element of the system transforms into national strength. Raksha Mantri underlined that military and administrative integration cannot proceed along separate paths, adding that, as joint and integrated structures develop, there will be a need for continuity and expertise across all areas - policy, administration, human resource management, financial processes, logistics, and institutional knowledge. He highlighted the importance of further enhancing structured cross-exposure between civilian and military officers, suggesting joint training programmes and developmental assignments for both sides to learn from each other’s experiences. “Military officers bring operational experience, a command perspective, and an understanding of warfare, while civilian officers contribute through administrative continuity, policy experience, an understanding of government processes, and institutional memory. When these strengths combine, decision-making becomes more informed, balanced, and effective,” stated Shri Rajnath Singh. Explaining with the example of ‘cyber warfare’, Raksha Mantri stated that if officers of the AFHQ Civilian Services develop defence-specific common cyber tools leveraging their expertise, it could prove beneficial to the Defence Forces. He added that a forum could be developed for the study of Indian military history, examining it from a civilian perspective, thereby fostering fresh ideas and new perspectives. He expressed confidence that, by leveraging expertise in such areas, the AFHQ Civilian Services will be able to make more meaningful contributions to the defence sector. Shri Rajnath Singh called upon the AFHQ Civilian Services to evolve into the “strategic brain” of India’s defence management architecture by developing a comprehensive understanding of the defence sector, functioning effectively in a joint environment, and continuously enhancing its expertise to face the emerging challenges. While he acknowledged the AFHQ Civilian Services for moving ahead in sync with changing times, he asserted that, at a time when modern warfare is driven by technological dynamism, the cadre must move beyond its specific mandate of proper implementation of service rules, regulations & orders. “A military derives its strength not merely from weapons and ammunition, but also from the thousands of unseen hands that always stand in their support. AFHQ Civilian Services is one of these unseen yet decisive forces. It must focus on strengthening the security architecture through research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas. Its active participation in core defence matters is essential as, being a permanent cadre of the Ministry of Defence, it possesses deep domain knowledge,” said Raksha Mantri. As part of the celebrations, Shri Rajnath Singh launched several digital initiatives of the office of Joint Secretary & Chief Administrative Officer (JS & CAO) and its Revised Vision & Mission Statement. The initiatives include Internet-Based Accommodation Management System (IBAMS) rakshaawas.caomod.gov.in portal; Integration of eHRMS with TULIP 2.0 System for processing of claims; Integration of CAO’s Office with TULIP 2.0 for processing of Pay & Allowances; and on-boarding on Smart Performance Appraisal Report Recording Online Window (SPARROW) portal. Raksha Mantri also released the 34th issue of the ‘Samvad’ magazine that contains travelogues, essays, articles, poems written by employees of various ranks posted in Service Headquarters and Inter-Service Organisations. He also presented awards to AFHQ personnel for their achievements in various fields such as sports, and some of the children of the employees who excelled in academics. Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay, Vice Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Additional Secretary Shri Manish Tripathi, JS & CAO Shri Amitabh Prasad and other senior officials were present on the occasion. AFHQ Day is celebrated on the first day of August every year to recognise the role of the personnel who work shoulder-to-shoulder with Service personnel, primarily in the three Integrated Service Headquarters, Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff and 24 Inter-Service Organisations of the Ministry of Defence. The foundation of AFHQ cadres was laid on August 01, 1942 by organising the then decentralised civilian posts/cadre operation as distinct entities under various Service Headquarters and Secretariat of Ministry of Defence and Finance (Defence) under the control of Chief Administrative Officer. **** VK/Sa vvy (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293732) आगंतुक पटल  : 691 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Marathi , Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Defence Military-civil integration key to a robust defence ecosystem to tackle emerging challenges: Raksha Mantri at AFHQ Civilian Services Day celebrations “‘Nation First’ a shared commitment of uniformed & civil services; Every element transforms into national strength if the objective is one” “AFHQ Civilian Services must evolve into strategic brain of India’s defence management; Research, geo-strategic thinking & innovative ideas vital for strengthening national security” प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia Meets Weightlifting Champion Mirabai Chanu Following Historic Commonwealth Triumph
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Development of North-East Region Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia Meets Weightlifting Champion Mirabai Chanu Following Historic Commonwealth Triumph Scindia Reaffirms Vision to Build the Next Generation of Sporting Champions in the Northeast In Line With PM Modi’s Vision Our North Eastern Region Must Produce Many More Mirabai Chanus Through World-Class Training and Support: Scindia प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi Fresh after scripting history with her record-extending third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow, ace weightlifter Mirabai Chanu called on Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, in New Delhi today. Congratulating Mirabai Chanu on her remarkable achievement, Shri Scindia praised her unwavering determination, discipline and perseverance, describing her success as an inspiration for millions of young athletes across the country, particularly in the North Eastern Region. During the interaction, Mirabai Chanu shared her inspiring journey of resilience and the challenges she overcame on her path to becoming one of India’s most celebrated sportspersons. The Minister also held detailed discussions with her on various aspects of sports, including training routines, nutrition, recovery cycles and the importance of adequate rest and sleep in achieving peak performance. The Minister also appreciated the invaluable contribution of Mirabai Chanu’s coach, trainer and physiotherapist, acknowledging that world-class sporting success is built on a strong support system backed by scientific training and expert guidance. Highlighting the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region’s vision for nurturing sporting talent, Minister Scindia discussed the development of a comprehensive sports ecosystem in the region through the establishment of the High Level Task Force (HLTF). Through this Task Force, the Ministry of DoNER is focusing on the ‘One State, One Sport’ initiative, under which each Northeastern state is being supported to develop excellence in sports where it has a natural competitive advantage, including disciplines such as weightlifting, archery and football. The Union Minister emphasized that the initiative is not merely about creating brick-and-mortar infrastructure, but about building a world-class sporting ecosystem centered on quality coaching, scientific training, sports science, nutrition, recovery and athlete support. He noted that providing aspiring athletes with access to high-quality training and facilities within the region itself would inspire many more young sportspersons to pursue excellence and enable the Northeast to produce many more champions like Mirabai Chanu. Chanu’s trainer, Vijay Sharma highlighted the potential of athletes from NER and acknowledged that these initiatives will help nurture grassroots athletes as well. In line with Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision for the Northeastern region, the meeting reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to strengthening the sporting ecosystem by investing in talent, coaching excellence and athlete development, while unlocking the immense sporting potential of the North Eastern Region. ***** PS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293757) आगंतुक पटल  : 216 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali-TR , Assamese , Manipuri , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Development of North-East Region Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia Meets Weightlifting Champion Mirabai Chanu Following Historic Commonwealth Triumph Scindia Reaffirms Vision to Build the Next Generation of Sporting Champions in the Northeast In Line With PM Modi’s Vision Our North Eastern Region Must Produce Many More Mirabai Chanus Through World-Class Training and Support: Scindia प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Mental Health of Students
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Mental Health of Students प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 8:14PM by PIB Delhi National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB) collects data on suicides from police recorded suicide cases. Comprehensive analysis of the data related to the accidental deaths and suicides in the country is published in the yearly Accidental Death & Suicide in India (ADSI) reports by National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB). As per ADSI Report, causes of student suicides include family problems, love affairs, illness, and failure in examination. Year wise, State wise, Gender and Age group wise details of student suicides are available in the ADSI reports which are accessible at https://ncrb.gov.in/accidental-deaths-suicides-in-india-year-wise.html . To address the issue of suicide, the Government is taking multi-pronged measures and provides psychological support to students, teachers and families for mental and emotional well-being to avoid incidences of suicide National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 recognizes that education must build character and enable learners to become ethical, rational, compassionate, and caring individuals while preparing them for gainful and fulfilling employment. The Policy emphasizes holistic and multidisciplinary education that promotes cognitive development, character building, creativity, and key 21st century skills. It aims to develop well-rounded individuals with deep knowledge in their chosen fields alongside capabilities across a range of disciplines. NEP 2020 also underscores the importance of promoting student wellness through physical fitness, good health, psychosocial well-being, and sound ethical grounding to support high-quality learning and reduce mental stress. An initiative of Ministry of Education, MANODARPAN, covers a wide range of activities to provide psychological support to students, teachers and families for mental and emotional wellbeing such as National toll-free helpline to provide guidance to callers through trained counsellor; live interactive sessions ‘Sahyog’ and Webinars ‘Paricharcha’ that are organized regularly to create awareness about the importance of mental health among all stakeholders, students in all States/UTs etc. These sessions are telecast on PM e-Vidya channels and are also available on ‘NCERT Official’ YouTube Channel. UGC has issued advisory to HEIs in January, 2023 circulating the National Suicide Prevention Strategy framed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. UGC also issued Guidelines on 13.04.2023, which provide for promoting physical fitness and sports activities for students; creating safeguards against academic pressure, peer pressure, behavioral issues, stress, career concerns, depression and other issues on the mental health of students; to teach positive thinking & emotions in the student community; and to promote a positive and supportive network for students. The Ministry of Education in July, 2023 has circulated a framework guideline on emotional and mental well-being of students in Higher Education Institutes (HEIs) with request to take proactive measures to incorporate the same in the institutional functioning and instil a feeling of confidence in the student community. The guidelines emphasised counselling services, early distress identification, suicide prevention SOPs, student support networks, strengthened grievance redressal mechanisms, and periodic institutional review to ensure sustained effectiveness. Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Centres (January 2024) has been issued by the Ministry of Education, which mandates student-support and protection measures such as counselling facilities, transparent fee structures, prohibition of batch segregation, and safeguards against practices that intensify academic pressure - extending mental-wellbeing protections beyond campuses. An Integrated approach for Promoting Positive Mental Health, Resilience, and Wellbeing has been conceptualized under the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme. Under this integrated approach, two fortnightly sessions are being held with faculty of higher education institutions to empower them to address student mental health concerns for early intervention. Annual National Wellbeing Conclaves were organised at IIT Hyderabad in November, 2024 and at IIT Bombay in November, 2025. A Regional Workshop on Mental Health was organized on 12-13 July 2026 at IIT Madras, which brought together institutional leaders, faculty, students, and mental health professionals to share best practices and strengthen campus wellbeing ecosystems. More than 4000 faculty have participated in online capacity building sessions, conclaves and regional workshop since May 2024. All IITs, IIMs, NITs and IIITs have put in place dedicated mental health or counselling centres within their campuses, staffed with full-time or visiting professional counsellors, clinical psychologists, and in some cases, psychiatrists. A large number of institutes often host mental health training sessions to raise awareness, reduce stigma, and educate students about mental health issues. These sessions cover topics such as stress management, coping strategies, and recognizing the signs of mental health issues. Some Institutes offers on/off-campus counselling services, where students can meet with mental health professionals. NEP 2020 envisages integration of skill development and vocational education with mainstream higher education to enhance employability, entrepreneurship and lifelong learning. AICTE is actively strengthening skill development by embedding it into technical education. It partners with industries and institutions to offer online skill courses aligned with the regular curriculum, along with skill-focused programmes, compulsory internships, and vocational degrees. To support skill development, the SWAYAM Plus portal has also been launched, focusing on upskilling and reskilling the workforce. More than 500 courses have been developed curated from 89 industry partners across 17 sectors and offered on emerging areas such as AI, Data Analyst etc. So far, more than 6,00,000 students registered on the platform. The National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) bridges the gap between academic learning and industry requirements by providing structured on-the-job training to graduates and diploma holders. The Scheme promotes industry-integrated education through Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programmes (AEDP), supports apprenticeships in emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), and facilitates academic credit integration through the NATS Assessment and Creditisation Framework.
