title: Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship Observes Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 with Enthusiastic Participation Across the Country
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship Observes Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 with Enthusiastic Participation Across the Country प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE) successfully observed Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 16 th July to 31 st July 2026, reaffirming its commitment towards the vision of Swachh Bharat Mission and promoting cleanliness, hygiene and environmental sustainability across all its offices, attached and subordinate offices, autonomous bodies and field institutions. The Swachhata Pakhwada was organised in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. During the fortnight, a wide range of activities were undertaken throughout the Ministry and its organisations to foster awareness and encourage active participation among officers, officials, trainees and stakeholders. The observance commenced with the Swachhata Pledge administered by Ms. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary (MSDE), where in officers and staﬀ reaffirmed their commitment towards maintaining cleanliness and promoting hygienic practices in their workplaces and surroundings. As part of the awareness initiatives, the Ministry organised various employee engagement activities including a Poster Making Competition and Slogan Writing Competition on the theme of cleanliness and environmental conservation. A workshop on "Curbing Single-use Plastic" was also organised to sensitise participants about sustainable alternatives and responsible waste management practices. In addition to above, tree plantation drive was also organised in Kaushal Bhawan. Saplings of indigenous tree species were planted by the all the senior officers to promote environmental conservation, enhance green cover and reinforce the message of sustainable development. The initiative reflected the Ministry's commitment towards fostering a cleaner, greener and environmentally responsible ecosystem. Addressing the occasion, senior officers of the Ministry emphasised that cleanliness is a shared responsibility and an essential component of creating safe, healthy and productive workplaces. They encouraged all employees and trainees to adopt cleanliness as a way of life and continue practising the principles of Swachhata beyond the Pakhwada. MSDE's attached offices, subordinate offices, autonomous bodies, and other training institutions actively participated in the campaign by organising plantation drives, awareness programmes, community outreach activities, cleanliness campaigns and behavioural change initiatives in collaboration with local communities. The Ministry also undertook extensive digital outreach through its official website and social media platforms by disseminating messages promoting cleanliness, sustainable practices and citizen participation in the Swachh Bharat Mission. The Ministry expressed its appreciation to all attached and subordinate offices, autonomous bodies and field institutions for their enthusiastic participation and successful implementation of the activities under Swachhata Pakhwada 2026. ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
title: Curriculum in ITIs
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Curriculum in ITIs प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi The Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE) offers vocational training programmes in 170 NSQF-compliant courses through a network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) across the country. All the courses offered through ITIs are aligned with the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) and approved by the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET). Curriculum revisions are carried out on a need basis in response to technological advancements, evolving occupational standards, and industry requirements or periodically, once every three years in accordance with NCVET guidelines. The curriculum review and revision process is a continuous and need-based exercise aimed at ensuring alignment with technological advancements and evolving industry requirements. The evaluation involves assessment of existing curricula with respect to emerging technologies, changing occupational standards, industry demand, employability trends, apprenticeship requirements, training outcomes, and feedback received during implementation. The curriculum revision process involves extensive consultations with stakeholders including State Governments/UT Administrations, industry representatives, Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs), subject matter experts, academia, employers, implementing agencies and other concerned Ministries/Departments, wherever required. Based on the evaluation and stakeholder consultations, curricula are revised to incorporate new technologies, Industry 4.0 applications, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), automation, green and renewable energy technologies, electric mobility, digital skills, entrepreneurship, workplace safety, environmental sustainability and outcome-based learning. Earlier, the curricula under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) were revised once every five years. After introduction of NEP 2020 and in accordance with NCrF guidelines, the curricula are being revised once in every three years. Presently, the curricula of 40 CTS courses have been revised. The revision of the remaining curricula will be undertaken on a demand basis, in consultation with all relevant stakeholders, taking into account technological advancements and industry requirements. DGT has taken following initiatives to encourage female enrolment in ITIs: Female candidates are eligible for admission to all NSQF-compliant courses under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) offered through ITIs, including 32 New age/ Future skill courses, based on the prescribed entry qualifications. Out of the 170 courses, seven (07) courses, namely Dress Making, Sewing Technology, Surface Ornamentation Techniques (Embroidery), Computer Aided Embroidery & Designing, Fashion Design and Technology, Cosmetology, and Spa Therapy, are women-centric under CTS. Government of India approved 30% reservation of seats for women candidates in all ITIs (Govt. & Private) in all courses and these seats could be filled based on the general reservation policy of each of the State/UTs. DGT has developed 32 New-Age courses/ Future Skill Courses for addressing the growing industry needs of the future ready job-roles in areas of Artificial Intelligence, Mechatronics, Electric Vehicles (EV), Industrial Robotics, Advanced Manufacturing, Internet of Things, Electronics, Semiconductor, Green Hydrogen & Renewable Energy and other emerging technologies.  In addition, new short-term, industry-oriented courses have also been developed to provide flexible upskilling and reskilling opportunities in response to changing industry demand and future workforce requirements. A list of these new-age courses under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) is at Annexure-I. The assessment of labour market demand for the introduction of new courses and revision of existing courses is undertaken through skill gap studies and continuous consultations with industries, Sector Skill Councils, District Skill Committees, employers, industry associations, State Governments, training institutions, and domain experts. Inputs on industry requirements, technological advancements, occupational standards, placement trends, apprenticeship opportunities, and emerging skill needs are duly considered during curriculum development and revision. This consultative mechanism ensures that the courses remain industry-relevant, enhance employability, and align with the evolving needs of the economy. ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
title: Skill Development For Healthcare Professionals
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Skill Development For Healthcare Professionals प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 4:09PM by PIB Delhi Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including Kerala. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills including in paramedical and allied healthcare sectors. PMKVY: Under the PMKVY, the Ministry supports training in job roles relevant to healthcare services. The major healthcare job roles under PMKVY 4.0 include Emergency Medical Technician-Basic, General Duty Assistant, Geriatric Caregiver (Institutional & Home Care), Healthcare Hygiene and Housekeeping Aide, Assistant Yoga Instructor, Panchakarma Assistant and Genetic Counselor. MSDE has launched the Training Programme for Multi-Skilled Caregivers under PMKVY, in line with the Union Budget 2026–27 announcements to skill 1.5 lakh caregiving professionals (1.3 lakh through MSDE ecosystem), creating a professionally trained workforce for healthcare, geriatric and home-based care while opening new employment opportunities, particularly for women and youth. NAPS: Under NAPS, apprenticeship opportunities are available across healthcare, paramedical, and allied healthcare sectors, based on the skill requirements of participating establishments. JSS: Under JSS Scheme, various healthcare-related skill development programmes are being implemented to enhance employability and livelihood opportunities, particularly for non-literate, neo-literate, school dropouts, etc. The healthcare-related courses offered under the JSS Scheme include Basic Health and Wellness Skills (Secondary School), Basic Health and Wellness Skills (Senior Secondary School), Fundamentals of POSHAK (Poshan Shiksha and Kaushal) for Anganwadi Karya Karta, Foundation Course in Healthcare, Front Line Health Worker, General Duty Assistant (GDA), Helpers for Hospitals and Nursing Homes, General Duty Attendant (GDA), Geriatric Assistant, and Optician. CTS: Under CTS, the Healthcare Sector trades being offered through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) include Dental Laboratory Equipment Technician, Geriatric (old age) Care, Health Sanitary Inspector, Physiotherapy Technician, Radiology Technician, etc. Coverage: Total number of candidates trained under the major skill development schemes of MSDE in paramedical and allied healthcare sectors since 2023-24 up to 30 th June 2026 are as under: Scheme India Kerala PMKVY 1,20,588 2,361 NAPS 31,491 1,063 JSS 7,712 260 CTS* 48,862 160 * Session 2023 to 2025 Programme under Ministry of Health & Family Welfare : As per Ministry of Health & Family Welfare one-year Post Basic Diploma programmes in various clinical specialties have been developed in the Residency Mode (Earn While You Learn) by the Indian Nursing Council (INC), to strengthen the clinical competencies of registered nurses and to address the growing demand for specialized nursing care. These programmes provide structured, competency-based clinical training while enabling nurses to continue working during the course. MSDE has established and operationalized seven Skill India International Centres (SIICs) in different states on a pilot basis to facilitate international employment opportunities for the Indian youth. Further, MSDE, through the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), is facilitating overseas employment opportunities for healthcare professionals through country-specific workforce mobility initiatives. These initiatives include candidate mobilisation, language and domain-specific preparation, assessment and selection processes, employer engagement and deployment support in accordance with destination-country requirements. Under these initiatives, healthcare professionals have been trained for overseas opportunities through programmes such as the Japan Technical Intern Training Programme (TITP) for Caregivers and the Israel Government-to-Government (G2G) Caregiver Programme. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Shri Jayant Chaudhary in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. *** SH (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293795) आगंतुक पटल  : 126 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Skill Development For Healthcare Professionals प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
title: Expansion of Skill Development Ecosystem
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Expansion of Skill Development Ecosystem प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres / institutes under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Sikhshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country. The SIM aims at enabling the youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills. Government is actively working to expand training opportunities across the country including in rural, tribal, and aspirational districts, by encouraging more training infrastructure, better coverage of underserved areas, and strengthening of skilling initiatives through the State Skill Development Missions. An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 was conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income- related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries. Further, various processes have been put in place under PMKVY across the training lifecycle to ensure enrolled candidates receive quality training in compliance with PMKVY guidelines. The processes help in concurrent monitoring of training centers and candidate skilling progress in training centers. Some of the major initiatives include: Aadhaar based enrolment of the candidates under PMKVY to avoid fake enrolments Daily candidate attendance monitoring through Aadhaar enabled biometric attendance system (AEBAS) - Training centers have been mandated to install AEBAS application in the tab/phone of candidates and trainers to mark attendance during the training duration. Payment to the training centers has been linked to attendance. Recently the biometric system has been replaced with face authentication system. Concurrent Monitoring of training centers and candidate skilling lifecycle progress by Call Validation, Surprise Visits of Centers etc. Outcome based payment to training centers A penalty matrix has been devised to penalize non-compliant entities as per the discrepancies observed after due diligence by the Monitoring Committee. In cases of severe non-compliance or any unethical practice like offering bribe, intimidating inspector/assessor etc a training center may be suspended for a period of six months or blacklisted from the skill ecosystem. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Shri Jayant Chaudhary in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. *** SH (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293793) आगंतुक पटल  : 111 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Expansion of Skill Development Ecosystem प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Government is actively working to expand training opportunities across the country including in rural, tribal, and aspirational districts, by encouraging more training infrastructure, better coverage of underserved areas, and strengthening of skilling initiatives through the State Skill Development Missions. An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 was conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income- related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries. Further, various processes have been put in place under PMKVY across the training lifecycle to ensure enrolled candidates receive quality training in compliance with PMKVY guidelines. The processes help in concurrent monitoring of training centers and candidate skilling progress in training centers. Some of the major initiatives include: Aadhaar based enrolment of the candidates under PMKVY to avoid fake enrolments Daily candidate attendance monitoring through Aadhaar enabled biometric attendance system (AEBAS) - Training centers have been mandated to install AEBAS application in the tab/phone of candidates and trainers to mark attendance during the training duration. Payment to the training centers has been linked to attendance. Recently the biometric system has been replaced with face authentication system. Concurrent Monitoring of training centers and candidate skilling lifecycle progress by Call Validation, Surprise Visits of Centers etc. Outcome based payment to training centers A penalty matrix has been devised to penalize non-compliant entities as per the discrepancies observed after due diligence by the Monitoring Committee. In cases of severe non-compliance or any unethical practice like offering bribe, intimidating inspector/assessor etc a training center may be suspended for a period of six months or blacklisted from the skill ecosystem. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Shri Jayant Chaudhary in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. *** SH (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293793)

Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. The SIM aims at enabling the youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills. In order to ensure active engagement of the industry and aligning the skill training programmes with emerging sectors, MSDE has inter-alia taken the following steps: National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space. NCVET recognises the industry bodies as the Awarding Bodies (ABs) and/or Assessment Agencies (AAs). The Awarding Bodies are expected to develop the qualifications as per the industry demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the National Classification of Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations. NCVET has approved 10209 qualifications as per the industry requirements, out of which 2975 qualifications are valid and active, and 7234 qualifications are archived. Directorate General of Training (DGT) is implementing Flexi MoU Scheme and Dual System of Training (DST) in collaboration with industries to provide training to ITI students in real industrial environment. DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech and other companies like IBM, Microsoft, Autodesk, AWS, Shell, etc. to ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills training in modern and green technologies. The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 envisages greater integration of vocational education with mainstream education and promotes seamless mobility between academic and vocational pathways. In line with this vision, the Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP), developed in collaboration with UGC and AICTE, enables students enrolled in degree and diploma programmes to undertake apprenticeship training as an integral part of their curriculum. The programme enhances employability, promotes outcome-based learning, strengthens industry-academia linkages and facilitates acquisition of industry-relevant skills. Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job-roles have been specially aligned with Industry 4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics, Mechatronics, Drone Technology, etc. for upcoming market demand and industry requirements. DGT has introduced new age /future skills courses under CTS to provide training in emerging areas such as 5G Network, AI Programming, Cyber Security, Drone Technology, Internet of Things, etc. Two (02) Indian Institute of Skills (IIS) have been established at Ahmedabad and Mumbai, in Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode, with an aim to align industry-ready workforce to emerging economic opportunities. 36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective sectors, have been set up which are mandated to identify the skill development needs of respective sectors. Details of the candidates trained/enrolled under various schemes of MSDE are given as under: PMKVY (since inception to 30.06.2026) JSS (Since 2018-19 to 30.06.2026) NAPS (Since 2018-19 to 30.06.2026) CTS / ITIs (Session 2018 to 2025) 16,541,679 36,58,020 52,98,397 1,07,42,151 Amongst the schemes of MSDE, placements were tracked under the Short-Term Training component of PMKVY only in the first three versions (PMKVY1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0) implemented from 2015-16 to 2021-22. Out of 56.89 lakh candidates that have been certified under Short-Term Training, 24.3 lakh candidates have been reported placed with a placement rate at 42.8%. Under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied career path with orientation through industry relevant skill courses that include the On-the-Job Training (OJT). The schemes of MSDE are demand driven and training centres under these schemes are set up or engaged on need basis. Details of the training centres set-up or engaged under the schemes of MSDE as on 30.06.2026 is as under: PMKVY 4.0 Centres (STT+SP) * JSS centers NAPS Establishments ITIs Govt. Pvt. 13,633 294 57,935 3,328 10,528 * Short-term Training (STT) and Special Projects (SP) up to 30.06.2026 Further, in order to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training in the country, Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM SETU) scheme inter-alia aims to upgrade 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) in a Hub and Spoke model, wherein upgradation includes smart classrooms, modern labs, digital content, and new courses aligned to industry needs. Also, it aims to augment capacity of five NSTIs located in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur, and Ludhiana, including setting-up sector-specific National Centres of Excellence for skilling, with focus on advanced training of trainers with global partnership. title: Government Strengthens Drug De-addiction and Awareness Initiatives in Jammu & Kashmir Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Drug De-addiction and Awareness Initiatives in Jammu & Kashmir Under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Over 1.20 Crore People Sensitised in Jammu & Kashmir; 8,565 Nasha Mukti Mitras Join the Campaign प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government is implementing the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) to prevent substance abuse through sustained awareness campaigns, de-addiction, rehabilitation and counselling services across the country. In the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir, the campaign has reached more than 1.20 crore people , including over 69.14 lakh youth and 51.20 lakh women , while 8,565 Nasha Mukti Mitras have joined the nationwide movement against drug abuse, as on July 29 this year. The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the campaign under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) . Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma shared the details in a written reply to Shri Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi in Lok Sabha. The House was informed that the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments, Union Territory Administrations, NGOs and Government Hospitals for preventive education, awareness generation, treatment, rehabilitation and capacity-building programmes to reduce drug demand across the country. The written reply further stated that the Ministry is supporting a comprehensive network of de-addiction and rehabilitation facilities in Jammu & Kashmir, including Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), 3 Outreach and Drop-In Centres (ODICs), 2 Community-Based Peer-Led Intervention (CPLI) programmes, 6 District De-Addiction Centres (DDACs), and 21 Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs) established in Government hospitals across the Union Territory. The House was also informed that the Ministry operates the National Toll-Free De-addiction Helpline 14446 , which provides primary counselling and referral services. The helpline has received more than 4.6 lakh calls across the country, including over 11,000 calls from Jammu & Kashmir , reflecting increased awareness and accessibility of support services. The reply further highlighted that the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan , launched on 15 August 2020 , has now been expanded to all districts of the country. The campaign focuses on educational institutions, universities and schools to create awareness against substance abuse through community participation. Nationally, the campaign has sensitised more than 29.05 crore people , including over 11.05 crore youth and 7.81 crore women , while more than 1.17 lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras have joined the movement. Replying to the query regarding assessment of the campaign, the House was informed that the implementation of NMBA is regularly reviewed through monthly review meetings, Chintan Shivirs and National-Level Conferences with States and Union Territories. States and UTs are encouraged to establish and regularly convene State, District and Block-level NMBA Committees to strengthen coordination and ensure effective implementation. These efforts have contributed to sustained awareness generation, increased community participation, stronger inter-departmental coordination, and improved outreach for prevention, treatment and rehabilitation services for persons affected by substance abuse. title: Creating a Premier Hospitality and Recreation Destination: How VCF-SC Enabled BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. to Expand Tourism and Employment
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Creating a Premier Hospitality and Recreation Destination: How VCF-SC Enabled BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. to Expand Tourism and Employment प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi The hospitality and tourism sector plays a vital role in driving economic growth, creating employment opportunities and promoting regional development. However, expanding businesses in this sector often requires substantial financial support to develop world-class infrastructure and meet growing customer expectations. Demonstrating how institutional support can accelerate entrepreneurial growth, BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. , established in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, owned by Manish Verma , has emerged as a leading destination for recreation, hospitality and social events. The company's journey reflects the transformative impact of the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. has established a modern amusement park featuring electrical and mechanical rides, water-based recreational activities, multi-cuisine dining facilities and a well-equipped banquet hall for weddings, conferences and social gatherings. With its quality infrastructure and integrated hospitality services, the enterprise has gained strong recognition and built a loyal clientele across the region. Mr. Manish Verma Recognising the project's potential to generate employment and contribute to the local economy, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹ 4.81 crore in 2015 through venture capital assistance comprising equity and optionally convertible debentures. The financial support strengthened the company's expansion plans and enhanced its operational capabilities. Integrated Amusement Park, Banquet Hall & Hospitality Services The financial assistance enabled the company to expand its existing business operations, strengthen community engagement, enhance premium wedding and event services under a unified business model and meet the increasing demand for quality hospitality services. The project also generated direct and indirect employment opportunities for local people while helping the enterprise establish a strong customer base in the competitive hospitality sector. Amusement Park Facility Integrated Amusement Park, Banquet Hall & Hospitality Services The impact of the intervention has been significant. Today, the enterprise has increased its total workforce from 14 to 25 employees , including 12 Scheduled Caste/Backward Class employees and 13 non-SC/BC employees . The company's asset base has also witnessed remarkable growth, increasing from ₹ 1.21 crore to ₹ 6.65 crore , reflecting sustained business expansion and improved financial strength. Mr. Manish Verma Reflecting on the journey, Mr. Verma said: "The support received under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, enabled us to expand our business, strengthen operational stability and enhance our hospitality and event services. Today, BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. has established a strong customer base and continues to generate employment while contributing to the growth of the hospitality sector in Uttar Pradesh." The success of BP Sons Pvt. Ltd. demonstrates how targeted financial support under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) is enabling Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish sustainable enterprises that generate employment, strengthen regional tourism and hospitality infrastructure and contribute to inclusive economic development. By fostering entrepreneurship and supporting business expansion, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to empower entrepreneurs, create livelihoods and build sustainable futures across the country. title: Driving Clean Energy and Sustainable Entrepreneurship: How VCF-SC Enabled Dartyens Power Pvt. Ltd. to Establish a Successful Solar Power Project
content:

                03 AUG 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi India's transition towards clean and renewable energy requires innovative entrepreneurs backed by timely financial support. Recognising the importance of promoting sustainable enterprises while creating employment opportunities, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been supporting Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs in establishing commercially viable businesses. One such success story is Dartyens Power Pvt. Ltd. , owned by Dasari Kumari, located in Nalgonda, Telangana , which has successfully established and operates a 1 MW Solar Power Plant , contributing to clean energy generation and regional economic development. Recognising the project's potential, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹ 4.35 crore in 2016 through venture capital assistance comprising equity and optionally convertible debentures . The financial support enabled the company to establish the solar power project and strengthen its long-term operational and financial sustainability. Ms. Dasari Kumari The financial assistance enabled Dartyens Power Pvt. Ltd. to successfully commission and operate a 1 MW Solar Power Plant , generating clean and sustainable energy while improving operational efficiency. The enterprise has consistently achieved its expected performance targets and generates stable revenue in line with planned financial projections. The project has also strengthened environmental sustainability by promoting renewable energy generation in the region. Solar Power Plant Sustainable Growth Through Renewable Energy The intervention has created a significant socio-economic impact. The enterprise is operating successfully with improved financial growth and has generated both direct and indirect employment opportunities for local people. It has also established strong market linkages with clients, ensuring sustained business expansion and long-term commercial viability while contributing to India's clean energy mission. Reflecting on the journey, Ms. Dasari Kumari said: "The support received under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, enabled us to establish our solar power project successfully. The assistance strengthened our business operations, improved financial sustainability and helped us generate clean energy while creating employment opportunities for the local community." The success of Dartyens Power Pvt. Ltd. demonstrates how targeted financial support under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) is empowering Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish sustainable enterprises in emerging sectors such as renewable energy. By supporting entrepreneurship, generating employment and promoting environmentally sustainable development, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to build inclusive growth and sustainable futures across the country. title: Expanding Access to Affordable Healthcare: How VCF-SC Enabled Aboli Hospital to Build a Modern Multi-Speciality Healthcare Facility
content:

                03 AUG 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi Dr. Anil Sadashivrao Kamble Quality healthcare is a cornerstone of inclusive development. However, access to advanced medical facilities remains a challenge for people living in semi-urban and rural regions. Demonstrating how entrepreneurship coupled with institutional support can bridge this gap, Aboli Hospital Private Limited , established by Dr. Anil Sadashivrao Kamble in Parbhani, Maharashtra, has emerged as a trusted multi-speciality healthcare institution. The hospital's journey reflects the transformative impact of the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Aboli Hospital Private Limited has established a 70-bedded multi-speciality hospital equipped with a pharmacy, advanced Intensive Care Unit (ICU) and critical care facilities capable of treating complex medical emergencies, particularly paralysis and other critical illnesses. The hospital provides quality and affordable healthcare services under one roof for the people of Parbhani and neighbouring districts. Recognising the project's social and healthcare impact, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹ 5 crore in 2023 through venture capital assistance comprising equity and optionally convertible debentures. The support also enabled the hospital to procure modern medical equipment, reduce the burden of high-cost bank loans and strengthen linkages with health insurance schemes, including Ayushman Bharat . Facility Multi-Speciality Hospital & Advanced Critical Care Facility The financial assistance enabled the hospital to establish modern healthcare infrastructure, strengthen advanced ICU and critical care services, procure state-of-the-art medical equipment and expand access to affordable healthcare for underserved communities. The institution has also developed strong linkages with government healthcare schemes, insurance providers and specialised medical practitioners, enhancing the quality and reach of healthcare services across the region. Multi-Speciality Hospital & Advanced Critical Care Facility The impact of the intervention has been significant. Today, the hospital has generated 65 direct employment opportunities , including 27 Scheduled Caste employees and 38 non-Scheduled Caste employees . The enterprise has witnessed remarkable financial growth, with its net worth increasing from ₹ 61.75 lakh to ₹ 6.93 crore , while creating assets worth ₹ 2.78 crore . The project has emerged as a model of inclusive healthcare entrepreneurship by providing affordable, quality medical services while creating sustainable livelihoods and strengthening healthcare delivery in the region. Today, Aboli Hospital stands as a trusted critical care and multi-speciality healthcare institution, improving access to advanced medical treatment across the region." By fostering entrepreneurship and promoting inclusive development, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to empower entrepreneurs, create livelihoods and ensure that essential healthcare reaches underserved communities across the country. title: 47,328 Villages Selected Under PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component Across the Country; 435 Villages in Telangana
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 47,328 Villages Selected Under PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component Across the Country; 435 Villages in Telangana Over 3.28 Lakh Development Works Identified and More Than 47.59 Lakh Beneficiaries Saturated Under the Scheme प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) to promote the socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste communities through the integrated development of villages under its Adarsh Gram Component . The scheme aims to ensure saturation of key socio-economic indicators through convergence of Central and State Government schemes while addressing critical development gaps. Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale , in a written reply to Shri Anil Kumar Yadav Mandadi in the Rajya Sabha, informed that 47,328 villages have been selected across the country under the Adarsh Gram Component of PM-AJAY, including 435 villages in Telangana . State-wise details of the selected villages have been placed on the Table of the House. The Minister further informed that the Adarsh Gram Component focuses on the integrated development of selected villages through the saturation of 50 monitorable socio-economic indicators across 10 development sectors , including education. A Need Assessment Survey is conducted to establish the baseline status of these indicators. The identified gaps are addressed through convergence with Central and State Government schemes or through interventions supported under PM-AJAY. Progress made by States and Union Territories is regularly updated through the PMAGY Portal . The House was also informed that, across the country, 3,28,131 development works and 1,10,51,213 beneficiaries have been identified under the scheme. Of these, 46,642 development works have been completed, while 47,59,399 beneficiaries have already been saturated through various interventions. With regard to Telangana , the written reply stated that under the education sector , 3,529 beneficiaries have been identified, of whom 472 beneficiaries have already received benefits under the scheme. Replying to a query regarding third-party audit, Shri Athawale informed that States and Union Territories have been directed to verify the self-declaration of Adarsh Gram villages under the PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component. Accordingly, validation is being undertaken by the respective State and UT Governments. The PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Component continues to promote inclusive and sustainable rural development by improving access to education, infrastructure, livelihoods and essential services, thereby contributing to the socio-economic empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities across the country. title: Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries “Quality Statistics as Driver of Change” प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi PRESS RELEASE- Day 1 The two-day meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices (NSO) of BRICS Member Countries was inaugurated under the Chairship of India on 03 August 2026 , at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India. The event brought together more than 350 participants including representatives from National Statistical Offices of BRICS, policy makers, academia, think-tanks, civil society organisation and technical experts. 2.         Guided under the overarching theme " Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability (BRICS), the BRICS Statistics track, India has adopted the theme " Quality Statistics as Driver of Change ”, reflecting an unwavering commitment to data quality, innovation, effective dissemination, and people-centric statistical systems that are responsive to rapid technological advancements, the growing demand for high-frequency and granular data, and the increasing reliance on official statistics to support evidence-based, sustainable, and inclusive development. 3.         The inaugural session of the Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices was initiated with an introduction by DG (Data Governance), MoSPI followed by an address by Shri Alok Kumar, Principal Secretary, Planning and Programme Implementation, Uttar Pradesh. 4.         Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI and Chair of BRICS 2026 Statistics Track welcomed the delegates to the two-day event and highlighted key priorities of the BRICS Statistics Track 2026 centered on "Quality Statistics as a Driver of Change” including modernizing national statistical systems, utilizing administrative data and digital public infrastructure, and enhancing data governance and privacy standards. He also emphasised that, through technical exchanges and shared experiences, BRICS member nations aim to bridge data gaps, drive evidence-based decision-making, and build resilient statistical systems for the future. 5.         During the inaugural session, Heads of NSOs and representatives of BRICS member countries of Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) also shared brief introductions and their expectations from the meeting. The participating countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation under the BRICS Statistics Track and underscored the importance of international collaboration in advancing official statistics. They emphasised that sustained cooperation through knowledge sharing, exchange of best practices, harmonisation of statistical methodologies, and promotion of statistical innovation would enable BRICS Statistical community to strengthen the evidence base for informed policymaking, foster resilient economies, and accelerate progress towards sustainable development. 6.         A draft BRICS Joint Statistical Publication (JSP), 2026 and Snapshot BRICS JSP 2026 were released on August 3, 2026 during the meeting.  Any additional inputs or comments from BRICS member countries shall be incorporated subject to consensus of BRICS member countries. 7.         The BRICS Main Technical Session-I, titled "From Digital Platforms to Execution-Level Experience: National Practices and Strategic Approaches for Data Dissemination," featured presentations by different member countries, namely India, Brazil, China, Egypt, Indonesia, Russia, South Africa and UAE. The presentations showcased national experiences, innovative approaches, and strategic initiatives aimed at strengthening data dissemination systems, enhancing accessibility, and promoting the effective use of official statistics in the digital era. 8.         The Technical Session-II on "Transformational Reforms in Statistical System" featured presentations by India, Ethiopia, Russia, South Africa, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), highlighting national reforms, institutional innovations, and strategies to modernise statistical systems in response to the rapidly evolving data ecosystem. 9.         Besides the Technical sessions, a side-event on the theme, ‘Unlocking the potential of Administrative Data’ was also held on August 03, 2026 in collaboration with knowledge partner CivicDataLab, which was attended by representatives from BRICS member countries, civil society organizations, academia and officers from Central and State Governments.  The session highlighted the growing role of administrative data as a strategic national resource for producing more timely, cost-effective, and granular official statistics, while emphasising the need for harmonised metadata, interoperable systems, and stronger institutional collaboration. The discussions concluded with a call for stronger collaboration among governments, National Statistical Offices, academia, and technology partners to build trusted data ecosystems and strengthen evidence-based policymaking. *** Samrat/Dileep/Sundaram (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293963) आगंतुक पटल  : 176 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries “Quality Statistics as Driver of Change” प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Modernization of National Sample Surveys through adoption of digital platforms such as Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) integrated with e- sigma platform incorporating in-built validation checks, AI-enabled ch...
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Modernization of National Sample Surveys through adoption of digital platforms such as Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) integrated with e- sigma platform incorporating in-built validation checks, AI-enabled chatbot, and multilingual interfaces Base revision of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI), and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) MoSPI has undertaken comprehensive data harmonisation/ standardisation initiatives which inter-alia includes adoption of National Metadata Structure (NMDS 2.0), introduction of Statistical Quality Assessment Framework (SQAF) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 2:51PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has undertaken several significant measures to strengthen the national statistical ecosystem. A major focus has been the modernization of National Sample Surveys through the adoption of digital platforms such as Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) integrated with e- sigma platform incorporating in-built validation checks, AI-enabled chatbot, and multilingual interfaces etc. MoSPI has launched short duration surveys to cater the emerging need for high-frequency socio-economic indicators. Furthermore, administrative datasets have been integrated for strengthening sampling frames for some surveys which improved survey efficiency and contributed to the timely compilation of official statistics. Significant reforms have also been undertaken in macroeconomic statistics, including base revision of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI), and Index of Industrial Production (IIP). MoSPI has undertaken comprehensive data harmonisation/ standardisation initiatives which inter-alia includes adoption of National Metadata Structure (NMDS 2.0), introduction of the Statistical Quality Assessment Framework (SQAF), alignment with national and international classification standards. MoSPI examines global statistical standards and best practices for its suitability in Indian context and possible adoption/adaptation in Indian statistical system, while undertaking measures to improve accuracy, transparency and credibility of statistical data. These, inter-alia, include adoption of the United Nations Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (UNFPOS) in May 2016, to promote good practices and professional ethics in production and dissemination of Official Statistics in the country. Other initiatives include adoption of Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) - 2018 Framework in the new series of Consumer Price Index (CPI) released on 12.02.2026 with 2024 as new base (from earlier base of 2012) and release of National Industrial Classification (NIC) 2025 aligned with International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC) Revision 5. In alignment with national and international best practices, MoSPI has also undertaken comprehensive data harmonization/ standardization initiatives which inter-alia include introduction of the Statistical Quality Assessment Framework (SQAF) which is based on the UN National Quality Assurance Framework (UN NQAF) 2019 providing a comprehensive framework to infuse greater efficiency, reliability and accountability. The underlying concepts and methodology of National Accounts is aligned with United Nations System of National Accounts, 2008. Moreover, CPI and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) follow the Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) of International Monetary Fund (IMF). MoSPI has also developed the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework (SDG-NIF) in close alignment with the UN’s Global Indicator Framework (GIF) established by the UN Statistical Commission. While modelled on the GIF, the NIF customizes indicators to suit India’s national priorities, policy contexts and data ecosystems. MoSPI has operationalised PAIMANA (Project Assessment, Infrastructure Monitoring & Analytics for Nation-building) for the mandated monitoring of Central Sector Infrastructure Projects replacing the erstwhile OCMS-2006 (Online Computerized Monitoring system). To further strengthen the efforts towards infrastructure monitoring, MoSPI has launched a Performance Monitoring Dashboard which provides the performance of key infrastructure sectors through a set of standardized indicators. The dashboard was launched on 16 th April 2026 to strengthen infrastructure monitoring and evidence-based policymaking to provide a comprehensive view of the performance of key infrastructure sub-sectors. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Rajya Sabha today. *** Samrat/ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293737) आगंतुक पटल  : 232 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Modernization of National Sample Surveys through adoption of digital platforms such as Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) integrated with e- sigma platform incorporating in-built validation checks, AI-enabled chatbot, and multilingual interfaces Base revision of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI), and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) MoSPI has undertaken comprehensive data harmonisation/ standardisation initiatives which inter-alia includes adoption of National Metadata Structure (NMDS 2.0), introduction of Statistical Quality Assessment Framework (SQAF) प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh inaugurates Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology at IIT Delhi
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh inaugurates Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology at IIT Delhi Five flagship initiatives launched to accelerate innovation, sustainability and digital transformation in India's handloom sector प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, today inaugurated the Centre of Excellence for Handloom Technology (CoE-HT) at IIT Delhi, marking a significant milestone in the Government's efforts to modernise India's handloom sector through technology, innovation and research. The inaugural ceremony was attended by Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Ministry of Textiles; Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms); Smt. The establishment of the Centre reinforces the Ministry of Textiles' commitment to preserving India's rich handloom heritage while equipping the sector with advanced technologies, research capabilities and innovation-led solutions. title: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates Commonwealth Games 2026 Weightlifting medallists with cash rewards; urges athletes to inspire next generation by visiting schools and colleges
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates Commonwealth Games 2026 Weightlifting medallists with cash rewards; urges athletes to inspire next generation by visiting schools and colleges प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 2:14PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, on Monday, felicitated India's Commonwealth Games 2026 weightlifting medallists, lauding their historic performances in Glasgow. Indian weightlifters competed in 11 weight categories and returned with eight medals – one gold, six silver and one bronze. The Indian contingent registered multiple Commonwealth Games and Commonwealth records, while several athletes also achieved personal-best lifts. The Hon’ble Minister presented cash awards of ₹30 lakh to gold medallists, ₹20 lakh to silver medallists and ₹10 lakh to bronze medallists in recognition of their outstanding achievements at the Commonwealth Games, where Indian weightlifters delivered one of the country's strongest campaigns. Congratulating the lifters, Dr. Mandaviya said that the entire nation had celebrated their achievements. "In Parliament too, announcements were made every time you won medals. Those moments made every Indian proud," he said. The Hon’ble Minister paid rich tributes to the coaches, including Dronacharya awardee Vijay Sharma, who was present on Monday during the felicitation, emphasising their indispensable role in shaping champions. "The guru has the biggest role in an athlete's journey. There is nothing greater than a coach's contribution in creating champions," he added. Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu created history by becoming the first Indian weightlifter to win three consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medals, while Rishikanta Singh and Valluri Ajay Babu set new Commonwealth Games records in the Snatch. Several lifters, including Gyaneshwari Yadav and Harjinder Kaur, registered personal-best performances. Out of the 11 weightlifters who competed, six of them are Khelo India Athletes (KIAs). Among the medallists, Gyaneshwari is a Khelo India athlete, while Bindyarani Devi, Harjinder and others train at the Sports Authority of India's National Centre of Excellence (NCOE) in Patiala, which plays an instrumental role in the success of India's grassroots and elite athlete development ecosystem. Calling upon athletes to become ambassadors of sport, the Hon’ble Minister also urged the weightlifters to visit schools and colleges to inspire young people to embrace sports. "Your stories can motivate thousands of children to dream big. Together, we are taking decisive steps towards building a truly sporting nation," he said. Dr. Mandaviya engaged with the weightlifters in conversations about their struggles, journeys to the podium and aspirations for future competitions, particularly the Asian Games 2026. The athletes shared stories of overcoming hardships, the support received through national coaching camps, international exposure and scientific training, and their determination to continue winning laurels for the country. Addressing those who narrowly missed the podium, Dr. Mandaviya encouraged them not to lose heart. "A sportsperson never truly loses. What matters is the passion to keep improving. I believe the blessings of Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the support of 140 crore Indians are always with you." Highlighting the Government's long-term vision for Indian sports, Dr. Mandaviya noted that many of the medallists had emerged through initiatives such as Khelo India, which provides young athletes with world-class coaching, scientific support and competitive exposure. "The country has invested in you because it believes in your potential. Every possible facility is being created so that Indian athletes may compete against the best in the world," he said. ***** Ayushman Kumar (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2293712) आगंतुक पटल  : 289 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Telugu , Kannada , Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Bengali , Bengali-TR , Gujarati , Tamil Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates Commonwealth Games 2026 Weightlifting medallists with cash rewards; urges athletes to inspire next generation by visiting schools and colleges प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Samudra Manthan – National Offshore Exploration Scheme Churning the Ocean for Energy प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                03 AUG 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi Samudra Manthan marks a decisive step in India's journey towards energy security and self-reliance. With a Phase-I outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to FY 2030–31, the scheme is designed to unlock India's vast offshore hydrocarbon potential. It focuses on accelerating exploration, deploying modern technology, creating shared infrastructure, and strengthening domestic manufacturing. It aims to add over 600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon reserves, raise domestic production, reduce import dependence, and build a globally competitive offshore energy ecosystem. A New Chapter in Offshore Exploration Energy powers every aspect of modern life. It fuels homes, farms, industries, transport, and the wider economy. As India continues its rapid growth, ensuring a reliable, affordable, and secure energy supply has become a national priority. While the country's energy needs continue to rise, a significant share of its crude oil and natural gas requirements is met through imports. Expanding domestic production is therefore essential to strengthen energy security, reduce import dependence, and conserve valuable foreign exchange. Among the country's key energy resources are hydrocarbons—organic compounds made of hydrogen and carbon. They occur deep below the land and the seabed. Crude oil and natural gas are the widely used hydrocarbons. They provide the raw material for petrol, diesel, LPG, petrochemicals, fertilisers, and numerous industrial products. India's offshore basins hold vast untapped hydrocarbon potential. A basin is a large natural depression in the earth where hydrocarbons collect.  Unlocking these resources requires modern exploration, reliable geological data, advanced drilling capabilities, and a strong domestic supply chain. To accelerate this effort, Samudra Manthan – the National Offshore Exploration Scheme has been approved on 31 July 2026. With a Phase-I outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to FY 2030‑31, it aims to boost the hydrocarbon exploration and production sector. Why The Seas Hold the Key for India India is the world’s third-largest consumer of crude oil . Its annual import bill is nearly USD 144 billion , or about ₹13 lakh crore . Recent global events have shown how vital uninterrupted energy access is. Higher domestic output has thus become critical for a rapidly growing economy. The Offshore Opportunity Much of India’s future oil and gas potential lies offshore. Deepwater and ultra-deepwater basins are sea zones with very high-water depth. India’s eastern and western offshore basins extend to water depths of up to 3,000 metres. They are estimated to hold over 5,600 MMTOE (Million Metric Tonnes of Oil Equivalent) of hydrocarbon potential. Recent finds in the Cauvery, Mahanadi, and Andaman basins have reinforced this promise. ONGC's Fixed Offshore Platform The Challenge of Deepwater Exploration Exploration is a costly and patient activity. Moving from the award of an exploration block to commercial production typically takes 5–10 years. A single deepwater exploratory well costs about USD 125–150 million. Such high stakes can discourage offshore exploration. There is another reason why constant search matters. Existing fields witness a natural decline of around 6–7 percent every year. New discoveries are needed simply to sustain current output. Sustained exploration thus serves as a path to lasting self-reliance in energy. Inside the Samudra Manthan Mission Samudra Manthan marks the transition from policy reform to mission-mode implementation. The scheme adopts a risk-sharing approach to attract sustained investment into frontier waters. It seeks to de-risk offshore ventures and encourage private capital, building enduring national capability across the value chain. In doing so, it converts a decade of reform into concrete action at sea. Components of Samudra Manthan Offshore exploration depends on reliable data, advanced technology, modern infrastructure, and a resilient supply chain. Samudra Manthan brings these elements together through four components. Seismic Data Acquisition, Processing, and Interpretation Limited offshore seismic coverage restricted the identification of drill-ready oil and gas prospects. The scheme funds large-scale 2D and 3D seismic surveys with an outlay of ₹ 28,534 crore . Advanced technology and Artificial Intelligence will speed up processing and interpretation. Older data in the National Data Repository will also be re-processed with modern tools. Accelerated Offshore Exploration High cost and long gestation make deepwater drilling a risky venture. To share this risk, the scheme allocates ₹ 43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells. Financial support covers up to 50 percent of eligible drilling cost, or ₹ 675 crore per well, whichever is lower. The scheme is open to both public and private Exploration and Production (E&P) operators to increase oil and gas reserves. It will accelerate reserve accretion and unlock India’s deepwater potential. Common Offshore Infrastructure Many offshore discoveries remain unproduced due to costly infrastructure, particularly in the Mahanadi and Kutch basins. The scheme provides ₹ 10,000 crore for shared production and evacuation facilities in select basins. Common infrastructure lowers project costs and turns idle finds into producing fields. Oil and Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone Low domestic manufacturing increases exploration costs, import dependence, and foreign exchange outflow. In view of this, an integrated Oil and Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone will be established with ₹ 2,000 crore . It will build domestic capabilities in manufacturing, repair, warehousing, engineering, and services. This directly advances Make in India across the supply chain. An amount of ₹ 350 crore supports monitoring, digital interventions, evaluation, human resources, awareness and outreach, events, and media. Component-Wise Allocation S. No. Component Amount (₹ Crore) 1 Offshore data acquisition 28,534 1A 2D seismic data acquisition for basin-wide coverage 12,000 1B 3D seismic data acquisition (and other techniques) 12,534 1C NDR data re-processing and AI tools implementation 4,000 2 Offshore exploration and infrastructure-led production 55,200 2A Offshore exploration acceleration 43,200 2B Infrastructure-led deepwater production and exploration 10,000 2C Development of oil and gas manufacturing and services zones 2,000 3 Monitoring and support activities 350 Total 84,084 An Integrated Enabling Ecosystem Beyond funding, the scheme creates a supportive environment for the entire value chain. Dedicated provisions cover: Digital programme management for transparent and efficient implementation Capacity building for professionals across the sector Adoption of cutting-edge technologies Continuous stakeholder engagement International outreach to attract global partners What Samudra Manthan Will Deliver The scheme is designed to create value for the economy and future generations. Subject to exploration success, it is expected to bring wide-ranging gains: Larger Reserves: Increase of over 600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon reserves, expanding the resource base from 1.6 billion to 2.2 billion Tonnes of Oil Equivalent (TOE). Higher Output: Annual domestic production is targeted to rise from around 62 MMTOE to 80 MMTOE. Incremental production of 10–15 MMTOE is expected, with a peak potential of 20 MMTOE. Lower Import Bill: Additional output can cut crude imports by nearly ₹1 lakh crore every year, generating significant foreign exchange savings. Investment and Growth: The scheme will promote investments across the value chain and drive strong GDP expansion. Employment: Large-scale jobs will be created in exploration, production, and allied activities. Indigenous Strength: Domestic manufacturing will deepen under Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, fostering a globally competitive ecosystem for offshore technologies. Together, these outcomes strengthen the country’s energy resilience. They also nurture technological leadership and long-term opportunities for industry and innovation. A Series of Reforms In recent years, India has steadily rebuilt its hydrocarbon exploration and production ecosystem. A series of structural reforms has made the sector open, transparent, and investor-friendly. Opening Up Offshore Acreage: More than 99 percent of the earlier “No-Go” areas have been removed. Over one million square kilometres of the Exclusive Economic Zone is now available for exploration. This zone is the sea area where India holds rights over natural resources. New Licensing Framework: The Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) was launched in 2016. Under it the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP) was launched which replaced the old nomination-based approach. HELP provides lower levies, uniform licensing, revenue sharing, and incentives to promote hydrocarbon exploration and early production. Simpler Contracts: India moved from Production Sharing Contracts (PSC) to Revenue Sharing Contracts (RSC) in 2016. In PSC, profits were shared between the Government and the contractor after recovery of cost. In RSC, the contractor bears all exploration risks, production and development costs in return for its stipulated share of revenue. Thus, this fiscal framework became simpler and more transparent, with less administrative intervention. Modern Law: The Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025 provided contractual stability and stronger dispute resolution. It recognised integrated petroleum operations and created a contemporary regulatory architecture. Enabling Rules: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025 operationalised these changes. They promote ease of doing business and streamline the administration of petroleum leases. Level Playing Field: The composition and mandate of the Empowered Committee of Secretaries were standardised across all contract regimes. Every operator now enjoys consistent treatment, whenever their contract was signed. Sharper Focus: The performance parameters of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India were reoriented towards exploration. This reinforces the national commitment to expanding the domestic resource base. Good exploration begins with good data. Seismic surveys send sound waves into the earth to map rock layers below the seabed. India has made sustained investments in such geoscientific knowledge through several national initiatives. These include Mission Anveshan, the National Seismic Programme, the Extended Continental Shelf Survey, the National Data Repository, and the Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study . Together, these have created one of the world’s most comprehensive geoscientific databases. The reforms have inspired visible confidence. Nearly 81 percent of active exploration acreage has been awarded after 2014. Under OALP, 172 blocks covering nearly 3.8 lakh square kilometres have been awarded. Committed investments in these blocks exceed USD 4.3 billion. Activity on the ground has gathered pace as well. During FY 2025‑26 alone, around 674 wells were drilled. Five new discoveries were made and seven discoveries were monetised. A New Chapter Begins in the Mahanadi Basin The hydrocarbon exploration reform journey reached a proud moment on 25 July 2026. Drilling of the first appraisal well commenced in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin. An appraisal well is drilled to further evaluate the quality and commercial value of the hydrocarbon discovery. The programme will deploy world-class deepwater drilling technology. The MN-DWN18-1-HD well is the first of four planned deepwater wells. These wells will systematically evaluate one of India’s most prospective offshore basins. The spudding (start of drilling a new well) marks the beginning of one of India’s most challenging deepwater campaigns. Every prospect evaluated and every well drilled will take the nation closer to self-reliance. Towards a Secure Energy Future India stands at the threshold of a promising energy era. The nation’s energy future doesn’t rest on a single discovery. It is being built through sustained reform, science, and the dedication of thousands of geologists, engineers, and offshore professionals. Samudra Manthan blends data, shared risk, common facilities, and homegrown capability into one mission. As the churn of the ocean begins, it carries the aspirations of a rising nation. Each step taken beneath the waves brings the country closer to a secure and self-reliant tomorrow.
